newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW discussing troubled parts plants.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW discussing troubled parts plants.

text.p: The future of a dozen parts plants that General Motors Corp considers uncompetitive are being discussed in the company's labor negotiations with the United Auto Workers, GM's top components executive said Tuesday.

J.T. Battenberg, president of GM's Delphi Automotive Systems unit, told reporters at an automotive supplier conference here that none of the 12 U.S. plants has improved its performance enough in recent months to be dropped from the company's list of troubled facilities.
"We're talking about them in negotiations and I really don't want to talk about any labor issues at this time," Battenberg said of the 12 plants.

GM has refused to identify the plants, but the list includes a door hinge and hardware plant in Flint, Mich., and an interior trim plant in Livonia, Mich., that the automaker intends to sell. UAW officials have identified the proposed buyer as Joseph, Littlejohn & Levy, a New York investment firm that owns other auto parts companies.

Battenberg declined to discuss the nature of the parts-related discussions with the UAW, but people close to the negotiations have said that GM wants to exclude several of the plants from job guarantees demanded by the union.
Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp in their pacts with the union agreed to guarantee jobs for 95 percent of their current UAW workforces.
UAW President Stephen Yokich said Monday that he believes GM can live with a contract that follows the same pattern.
